objective.value: Develop platform Escherichia coli strains for the bio-based production of multiple short-chain primary amines (SCPAs) by designing biosynthetic pathways through a combined retrobiosynthesis and precursor selection strategy, and demonstrate SCPA production in vitro (purified VlmD), in vivo (precursor feeding), and de novo from glucose, including enhanced iso-butylamine and ethylamine production.

hypothesis.value: Two explicit hypotheses: (1) amino acids would serve as ideal precursors of SCPAs because their metabolic pathways are well characterized and can be engineered to carry high fluxes; (2) valine decarboxylase (VlmD), if sufficiently promiscuous, might convert other amino acid precursors into the corresponding SCPAs. Decarboxylation was additionally expected to serve as a driving force for metabolic fluxes because it is irreversible.
hypothesis.notes: Hypotheses are stated by the authors prior to experimental validation; they are author expectations, not verified mechanisms.

value.in_vitro: VlmD converted 12 of 13 amino acid precursors to corresponding SCPAs; glycine to methylamine showed no activity; near or above 80% conversion for L-2-aminobutyrate, L-norvaline, L-valine, L-isovaline, L-isoleucine and 1-aminocyclohexanecarboxylic acid (product pairing for the latter conflicts with Fig. 3 caption; see conflicts)

experiments.name: Retrobiosynthesis and precursor selection for 15 SCPAs
objects: 15 target SCPAs (methylamine, ethylamine, n-propylamine, iso-propylamine, n-butylamine, iso-butylamine, (R)-sec-butylamine, tert-butylamine, n-amylamine, iso-amylamine, 2-methylbutylamine, cyclopentylamine, cyclohexylamine, aniline, benzylamine)
experiments.intervention: In-house retrobiosynthesis with 84 SMARTS reaction rules; precursor filtering by molecular type (amino acids retained) and by relative position of functional groups vs L-valine/L-leucine/L-isoleucine
experiments.conditions: PubChem MeSH Tree via PubChemPy v1.0.4; RDT v1.5.1
experiments.readouts: 4-21 precursors predicted per SCPA; 1-5 amino acid precursors per SCPA; best precursor identified for 13 SCPAs; tert-butylamine and aniline excluded (no suitable amino acid precursor)
experiments.outcomes: 13 SCPAs carried forward; EC 4.1.1.- (decarboxylase) identified as candidate enzyme class; VlmD selected as proof-of-concept enzyme

experiments.name: In vitro enzyme assay of purified His-tagged VlmD on 13 amino acid precursors
experiments.intervention: Incubation of purified VlmD with each precursor
experiments.conditions: 50 mM potassium phosphate buffer pH 7.5, 1 mM amino acid precursor, 0.1 mM PLP, 150 µg/mL VlmD, 2 h, 37 °C
experiments.readouts: HPLC (OPA derivatization) conversion percentages; LC-MS product confirmation (Supplementary Fig. 2, not provided)
experiments.outcomes: 12 of 13 precursors converted; glycine to methylamine inactive; 6 substrates at >= ~80% conversion

experiments.name: In vivo SCPA production by PA01 feeding 12 direct precursors
experiments.intervention: Individual feeding of 2 g/L of each of 12 amino acid precursors
experiments.conditions: MR medium pH 7.0 + 10 g/L glucose; 300 mL baffled flask, 50 mL, 37 °C, 200 rpm, 36 h
controls: no explicit negative control described in main text
experiments.outcomes: 10 SCPAs produced (76.28-1289.18 mg/L); n-amylamine and benzylamine not produced; residual L-norleucine 1.92 g/L and L-2-phenylglycine 1.82 g/L of 2 g/L fed (Supplementary Fig. 3, not provided)

experiments.name: De novo ethylamine production from glucose (EA01 vs NC01)
experiments.intervention: Overexpression of codon-optimized alaD (G. stearothermophilus) in PA01 background
experiments.conditions: MR medium pH 7.0 + 20 g/L glucose; 37 °C, 200 rpm, 48 h
controls: NC01 (control, no vlmD; exact genotype in Supplementary Table 2, not provided)
experiments.outcomes: 2.89 mg/L ethylamine; 22.78 mg/L L-alanine secreted as byproduct

experiments.name: De novo iso-butylamine production from glucose (iBA01 vs NC02)
experiments.intervention: Expression of vlmDopt in L-valine-overproducing Val (pKBRilvBNCED)

experiments.name: Fed-batch fermentation of iBA02 (sRNA knockdown, no supplementation)

source_locations.quote: Here, we report the development of platform Escherichia coli strains for the production of various SCPAs.
we report a strategy combining retrobiosynthesis and precursor selection step to design biosynthetic pathways for multiple short-chain primary amines (SCPAs)
it was hypothesized that amino acids would serve as ideal precursors of SCPAs
It was hypothesized that valine decarboxylase, if it is promiscuous enough, might be able to convert other amino acid precursors into the corresponding SCPAs of our interest.
E. coli WL3110 strain, which is a lacI knockout mutant of E. coli W3110, was used as a host strain for the production of SCPAs.
E. coli PA01 was constructed by transforming E. coli WL3110 with the plasmid pTac15-vlmDopt harboring the codonoptimized S. viridifaciens vlmD gene
the E. coli iBA02 strain was constructed by transforming the pTac15-vlmDopt-anti-ilvA-leuA-panB into the WLGBH (pKBRilvBNCED) strain
The resulting E. coli EA01 strain simultaneously overexpressing the codon-optimized vlmD and alaD genes
the corresponding biosynthetic genes, ilvA, leuA and panB, respectively, were deleted to remove the competing pathways during the course of strain optimization
leuABCD genes, all involved in the L-leucine biosynthesis, were additionally overexpressed in the iBA01 strain to increase the precursor, L-leucine, resulting in the iAA01 strain.
pTac15-vlmDopt-anti-ilvA-leuApanB was constructed by Gibson assembly
we knocked down the expression of these three genes by employing synthetic small regulatory RNAs (sRNAs)
rational protein engineering of VlmD was conducted to improve its activity toward L-alanine as a proof-of-concept target

84 reaction rules were constructed by manually extracting meaningful chemical transformation patterns on the basis of the third-level enzyme commission (EC) numbers from all the biochemical reactions available at the KEGG database
in vitro enzyme assays were first performed using the purified His -tagged VlmD
By individually feeding 2 g L−1 of the 12 corresponding precursors, the PA01 strain produced 10 SCPAs in vivo
(a) ethylamine from the NC01 (control) and EA01 strains; (b) iso-butylamine from the NC02 (control) and iBA01 strains; and (c) iso-amylamine from the NC03 (control) and iAA01 strains
Black and red lines in the left graph for each SCPA indicate chromatograms from in vitro enzyme assays without VlmD (control) and with VlmD, respectively.
the NC02 strain, a control strain which is the Val (pKBRilvBNCED) strain harboring an empty plasmid without the vlmD gene
1.5 mL of the seed culture was transferred to a 300 mL baffled flask containing 50 mL of culture medium, then cultivated at 37 °C and 200 rpm in a shaking incubator.
Fermentation was performed at 30 °C, and the culture pH was adjusted to 7.0 by adding 28% (v/v) ammonia solution.
The dissolved oxygen (DO) level was kept at 40% of air saturation by automatically controlling the agitation speed from 200 to 1000 rpm
The MR medium (pH 7.0) contains (per liter): 6.67 g KH2PO4, 4 g (NH ) HPO , 0.8 g MgSO4·7H2O, 0.8 g citric acid, and 5 mL trace metal solution

The NM2 medium contains per liter: 50 g glucose, 30 g CaCO3, 12.5 g (NH4)2SO4, 4.0 g KH2PO4, 2.0 g MgSO4·7H2O ... yeast extract, 0.262 g L-isoleucine, 0.262 g L-leucine, 0.425 mg sodium Dpantothenate, and 5 mL trace metal solution.

The NM3 medium contains per liter: 20 g glucose, 20 g (NH4)2SO4, 2 g KH PO , 0.4 g MgSO ·7H O, 1.6 g NaCl, 5 g yeast extract, 0.262 g L-isoleucine, 0.262 g L-leucine, 0.362 mg sodium D-pantothenate, and 5 mL trace metal solution.
supplemented with 1 mM of an amino acid precursor ... 0.1 mM of PLP, and 150 μg mL−1 of the purified His -tagged VlmD
By individually feeding 2 g L−1 of the 12 corresponding precursors
kanamycin (Km), 25 μg mL−1; and ampicillin (Ap), 50 μg mL−1
The PA01 strain was cultured for 36 h, and the EA01 strain was cultured for 48 h.
The enzymatic reaction was carried out for 2 h at 37 °C.
induced by adding 1 mM of isopropyl -D-1-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG) after 3 h. Cells were collected after additional 5 h of cultivation
Experiments were conducted in triplicates. Data are presented as mean values ± s.d.
All the flask cultures were repeated three times.
Another fed-batch fermentation profile of the iBA02 strain, which was conducted for the reproducibility, is available in Supplementary Fig. 5.
Automatic precolumn derivatizations of the 13 SCPAs were performed by using o-phthaldialdehyde (OPA; Sigma, St. Louis, MO) in HPLC.
The SCPAs produced from the in vitro enzyme assay reactions were further confirmed by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) analysis

Cell growth was monitored by measuring the optical density at 600 nm (OD600) using Ultrospec 3000 spectrophotometer (Amersham Biosciences, Uppsala, Sweden). Glucose concentration was determined using the glucose analyzer (model 2700 STAT; Yellow Springs Instrument, Yellow Springs, OH).
performed in a 6.6 L bioreactor (Bioflo 3000; New Brunswick Scientific Co., Edison, NJ)
analyzed using HPLC (1100 Series HPLC; Agilent Technologies) connected with MS (LC/MSD VL; Agilent Technologies)
Reaction decoder tool (RDT) (v1.5.1) was used for this purpose.

A homology model of VlmD was generated using GAD67 from Homo sapiens (PDB ID: 2OKJ). GAD67 was used as a template because it showed the greatest sequence identity (19.76%) with VlmD among proteins that use PLP as a cofactor.
analyzed using Microsoft Excel 2013 (15.0.5111.1000) and OriginPro 2019
the PA01 strain produced 10 SCPAs in vivo (Fig. 5): 76.28 mg L−1 of ethylamine, 873.31 mg L−1 of n-propylamine ... and 105.82 mg L−1 of cyclohexylamine.

the iBA02 strain was able to produce 10.67 g L−1 of iso-butylamine with a productivity of 0.36 g L−1 h−1, without the amino acid and vitamin supplementation, although the yield was slightly decreased to 0.057 g g−1

the EA01-V94I strain equipped with the V94I mutant of VlmD produced 5.69 mg L−1 of ethylamine from glucose. Although still low, this titer is 96.9% higher than that (2.89 mg L−1) obtained with the EA01 strain harboring the native VlmD

experiment_workflow.value_roles_note: Predicted precursors (EXP1) are design-stage values; measured titers are final measured values; no planned-vs-implemented discrepancies were reported.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Authors actively selected amino acids as the precursor molecular class for pathway construction (Q1: design choice; Q2: performed in this study; Q3: an actual design decision shaping all subsequent constructs, not a measurement).
ddr_annotations.design_action: From 4-21 retrobiosynthesis-predicted precursors per SCPA (classes: amino alcohols, amino acids, SCPAs, alkyl-CoA, hydrocarbons), select amino acids (proteinogenic and nonproteinogenic) as the precursor molecular type.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Amino acid pathways are well characterized and engineerable to high fluxes (refs 21,22); amino alcohol/SCPA/alkyl-CoA pathways poorly characterized; short-chain hydrocarbons considered harder to produce microbially (refs 23,24).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Retrobiosynthesis predicted multiple chemically diverse precursor classes for each of the 15 SCPAs, requiring a narrowing step before experiments (results_p001).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent + author_assertion; the superiority of amino acids over other classes was not experimentally compared in this paper.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Choice justified by cited prior amino-acid metabolic engineering literature, not by new measurements in this study.

generalizable_rule.rule: When retrobiosynthesis predicts multiple precursor classes for a target chemical, restricting to precursor classes with well-characterized, high-flux biosynthetic pathways (here: amino acids) is a workable pathway-design heuristic.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: 15 SCPA targets in E. coli with a PLP-dependent decarboxylase (VlmD); amino-acid route validated for 12/13 precursors in vitro and 10/12 in vivo
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Other precursor classes were not experimentally compared; other enzyme classes, hosts and product families untested

alternatives_considered: amino alcohols, SCPAs and alkyl-CoA precursors (rejected: pathways poorly characterized)
hydrocarbons (rejected: considered more challenging to produce microbially than amino acids)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Selection of VlmD as the proof-of-concept promiscuous enzyme is an active design choice by the current authors (Q1-Q3 pass).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Select valine decarboxylase (vlmD, Streptomyces viridifaciens), an EC 4.1.1.- decarboxylase, as the proof-of-concept promiscuous enzyme for SCPA production.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: All selected amino acid precursors were predicted convertible by EC 4.1.1.- enzymes; decarboxylation is irreversible and expected to drive flux; VlmD was previously reported to convert L-valine, L-leucine and L-isoleucine to iso-butylamine, iso-amylamine and 2-methylbutylamine (ref 28).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Retrobiosynthesis assigned third-level EC 4.1.1.- (reaction rule #51) to all amino-acid-precursor conversions (results_p003).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent (ref 28 substrate report) + mechanistic expectation of irreversibility (ref 25); promiscuity toward the other 10 precursors was a hypothesis tested afterward, not prior evidence.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Enzyme chosen by analogy to its previously reported substrates; the irreversibility argument is textbook knowledge (ref 25), not new mechanistic evidence.

generalizable_rule.rule: A promiscuous enzyme with reported activity on structurally related substrates (same functional-group layout) can serve as a proof-of-concept catalyst for converting additional analog precursors predicted by retrobiosynthesis.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: VlmD on 13 amino acid precursors in vitro (12 active) and 12 in vivo in E. coli WL3110 (10 produced)
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Other EC 4.1.1.- enzymes explicitly noted as examinable but not tested; non-amino-acid substrates; other hosts

alternatives_considered: other enzymes having EC number 4.1.1.- (mentioned as examinable, not tested)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: The functional-group relative-position criterion is an explicit, author-applied design filter that selected one precursor per SCPA (Q1-Q3 pass).
ddr_annotations.design_action: For each SCPA, select the single amino acid precursor whose amine/carboxyl relative positions match those of the known VlmD substrates L-valine, L-leucine and L-isoleucine (using RDT).
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Reaction feasibility is affected by electron-configuration changes with functional-group position relative to the reaction center (ref 29); functional-group positions affect substrate binding in the enzyme active site (ref 30).
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: 1-5 amino acid precursors per SCPA remained after molecular-type filtering, requiring a further selection criterion (results_p004).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=literature_precedent (refs 29,30) for the criterion; its predictive value was then supported experimentally (12/13 in vitro success), which is a screening result, not a mechanistic proof.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Criterion grounded in stated physical-organic and binding reasoning established before the experiments; however the underlying citations are external, so the mechanistic basis is borrowed rather than demonstrated here.

generalizable_rule.rule: Matching the relative positions of functional groups (distance to the reaction-center carbon) between candidate precursors and an enzyme's known substrates is a useful precursor-selection criterion for promiscuous-enzyme pathway design.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: 13 SCPAs with VlmD; 12/13 selected precursors converted in vitro; 10/12 produced in vivo
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: tert-butylamine and aniline (no matching precursor; dropped); other enzymes and other functional-group chemistries untested

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Overexpression of alaD to supply L-alanine from glucose is an implemented engineering action chosen by the authors (Q1-Q3 pass).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Introduce codon-optimized Geobacillus stearothermophilus alaD (alanine dehydrogenase) into PA01, creating EA01, to convert pyruvate to the L-alanine precursor for de novo ethylamine production.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Alanine dehydrogenase converts pyruvate to L-alanine (ref 31); alaD codon-optimized for heterologous expression in E. coli.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Goal of de novo production from glucose without external precursor feeding, after precursor-feeding proof of concept (results_p033).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement for enzyme function from cited literature (ref 31) and confirmed in this study by ethylamine detection; design rationale itself is enzyme-function knowledge.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Direct enzyme-catalyzed precursor supply; mechanism stated before construction.

generalizable_rule.rule: Overexpressing a dehydrogenase that forms the amino acid precursor from a central metabolite (e.g., AlaD: pyruvate to L-alanine) can enable de novo SCPA production from glucose in a vlmD-expressing host.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: EA01 (WL3110, vlmDopt + alaDopt), flask, MR + 20 g/L glucose; 2.89 mg/L ethylamine with 22.78 mg/L residual L-alanine
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Low VlmD activity toward L-alanine left most precursor unconverted; flux balancing untested; other precursors/hosts untested

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Using the previously developed L-valine overproducer Val (pKBRilvBNCED) as chassis for iBA01 is an implemented design choice (Q1-Q3 pass).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Transform the L-valine-overproducing E. coli Val (pKBRilvBNCED) strain (from ref 21) with pTac15-vlmDopt to create iBA01 for de novo iso-butylamine production.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: The Val strain already carries high flux toward L-valine, the direct precursor of iso-butylamine; the strain was available from the authors' previous work.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Need for an L-valine supply from glucose for de novo iso-butylamine production (results_p034).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (L-valine overproduction previously demonstrated; iso-butylamine production measured here).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Paper explicitly states the Val strain was 'previously developed' by the authors; reuse of an existing overproducer is the stated basis.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Additional leuABCD overexpression in iBA01 to create iAA01 is an implemented engineering action (Q1-Q3 pass).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Overexpress the leuABCD operon (L-leucine biosynthesis) in iBA01 to increase L-leucine supply, yielding iAA01 for de novo iso-amylamine production.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: leuABCD genes are all involved in L-leucine biosynthesis; L-leucine is the direct precursor of iso-amylamine.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Need to supply the L-leucine precursor from glucose for iso-amylamine production (results_p037).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (iso-amylamine detected), though pathway function is standard pathway knowledge.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Direct pathway-based precursor supply reasoning stated at design time.

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Replacing gene knockouts with synthetic sRNA knockdown of ilvA/leuA/panB to remove auxotrophies is an explicit, implemented design decision with a stated prior problem (Q1-Q3 pass).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Knock down (not knock out) ilvA, leuA and panB using synthetic sRNA cassettes (pTac15-vlmDopt-anti-ilvA-leuA-panB) in the prototrophic parental background WLGBH (pKBRilvBNCED), creating iBA02.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Knockdown reduces competing pathways while retaining the biosynthetic capacity that knockout removes, thereby eliminating the L-isoleucine/L-leucine/D-pantothenate auxotrophies of the Val-derived iBA01.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: iBA01 is auxotrophic for L-isoleucine, L-leucine and D-pantothenate because ilvA, leuA and panB had been deleted in the Val strain; this 'poses a problem in industrial fermentation' and required supplementation in fed-batch (results_p034, results_p047, results_p048). Trigger precedes the iBA02 construction.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement: iBA02 fed-batch without supplementation reached OD600 60.5 and 10.67 g/L iso-butylamine vs iBA01 with supplementation; sRNA technology itself from ref 32.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The knockdown-vs-knockout logic (retain residual gene function to preserve prototrophy while reducing competing flux) is stated in the paper at design time.

generalizable_rule.rule: When a production strain's competing-pathway deletions cause auxotrophies requiring costly supplementation, synthetic sRNA knockdown of the same genes in a prototrophic parent can remove the auxotrophies while maintaining or improving production.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: ilvA/leuA/panB knockdown in E. coli WLGBH (pKBRilvBNCED) + vlmDopt; fed-batch NM3 without supplementation; 10.67 g/L iso-butylamine, higher OD, slightly lower yield (0.057 vs 0.062 g/g)
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Single target product (iso-butylamine) and one gene set tested; knockdown strength tuning not reported; yield trade-off observed but not resolved

alternatives_considered: gene knockout of ilvA, leuA, panB as in Val (pKBRilvBNCED) (rejected because it causes the auxotrophies)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Rational engineering of VlmD toward L-alanine (12 designed single mutations) is an implemented, structure-guided design decision (Q1-Q3 pass).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Build a VlmD homology model (SWISS-MODEL, GAD67/2OKJ template), dock PLP-L-alanine (AutoDock Vina), select 6 active-site residues appearing to interact with L-alanine, and test 12 single substitutions toward larger side chains (V94I, V94L, V114I, V114L, T397A, T397V, W399L, S431T, S431V, S431L, D515K, D515N) identified from 250 BLASTP homologs.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: L-alanine is smaller than VlmD's preferred substrates; larger residues in the active site were expected to reduce active-site volume and increase interaction with the smaller substrate.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: VlmD showed the lowest in vitro conversion efficiency toward L-alanine among the 12 active substrates (Fig. 3), and EA01 secreted more L-alanine (22.78 mg/L) than ethylamine produced (2.89 mg/L) (results_p033, results_p049). Both observations precede the engineering.
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=structural_prediction + computational_prediction (homology model with 19.76% identity template; docking) guiding the design; predictions required and received experimental testing (flask screen of 12 variants).
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: Active-site-volume reasoning stated before variant construction; however it rests on a predicted (not experimentally determined) structure, so the mechanistic basis is model-based.

generalizable_rule.rule: For a PLP-dependent decarboxylase with poor activity toward a smaller-than-preferred substrate, introducing larger active-site residues to reduce pocket volume can improve activity toward the smaller substrate.
generalizable_rule.tested_scope: VlmD toward L-alanine in E. coli WL3110 flask cultures; best variant V94I gave 5.69 mg/L ethylamine (+96.9% over native); absolute titer remains low
generalizable_rule.excluded_scope: Only 12 single mutations at 6 residues tested; combinations untested; other enzymes/substrates untested; structural basis not experimentally confirmed

alternatives_considered: 12 candidate substitutions were compared experimentally; 11 performed worse than V94I (per-variant titers only in Fig. 8b/Source Data, not provided)

ddr_annotations.decision_type_rationale: Subjecting iBA01 to fed-batch fermentation in NM3 is an implemented bioprocess design decision (Q1-Q3 pass).
ddr_annotations.design_action: Scale iBA01 from flask to fed-batch fermentation in NM3 medium with DO-stat control and manual glucose feeding, supplementing L-isoleucine, L-leucine and D-pantothenate.
ddr_annotations.design_action_rationale: Stated rationale: iBA01 showed efficient iso-butylamine production without L-valine byproduct in flask cultivation.
ddr_annotations.trigger_observation: Flask result: iBA01 produced 1155.74 mg/L iso-butylamine with no L-valine byproduct (results_p034, results_p047).
ddr_annotations.evidence_grading_rationale: evidence_basis_type=experimental_measurement (flask performance) as the basis for scale-up; outcome measured in fed-batch.
ddr_annotations.reason_nature_rationale: The strain was advanced to scale-up because it was the best-performing, cleanest producer among the de novo strains; mapped to screening_derived because selection was based on measured comparative performance.

1-aminocyclohexanecarboxylic acid is converted to cyclohexylamine, and 1-aminocyclopentanecarboxylic acid to cyclopentylamine (Fig. 3 caption, results_p032; consistent with methods_p004 precursor list and chemical logic)
conflicts.conflict_reason: The Results text pairs the >=80% conversion of 1-aminocyclohexanecarboxylic acid with cyclopentylamine, whereas the Fig. 3 caption pairs cyclopentylamine with 1-aminocyclopetanecarboxylic acid (panel j) and cyclohexylamine with 1-aminocyclohexanecarboxylic acid (panel k). Substrate-product identity cannot be silently resolved from available sources.
conflicts.review_action: Check the original Fig. 3 panels and Source Data; the caption mapping is chemically consistent (ring size retained), suggesting a Results-text wording error, but this requires human verification.
